I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Spain (Madrid) is in the CET/CEST timezone. In late September, Spain is still on summer time (CEST = UTC+2), as the clocks change on the last Sunday of October.

ET (Eastern Time) in late September is EDT = UTC−4.

So the difference between Madrid (UTC+2) and ET (UTC−4) is **+6 hours**.

5:00 PM ET + 6 hours = 11:00 PM Madrid time, same date.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Peru (Lima) is in the **UTC-5** time zone and does not observe daylight saving time.

So I subtract 5 hours from 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026:

12:00 UTC − 5 hours = **07:00 local time**, same date.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is Central European Summer Time, which is UTC+2.

Tokyo is JST, which is UTC+9.

The difference is 9 - 2 = +7 hours ahead of CEST.

So 9:00 AM CEST on June 1, 2026 → add 7 hours → 16:00 JST on June 1, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT is UTC−7. Madrid in October is on CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2. However, I need to check whether daylight saving time has ended by October 11 in Spain.

Spain switches back to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So on October 11, Spain is still on CEST (UTC+2).

Difference: PDT (UTC−7) to CEST (UTC+2) = +9 hours.

October 11 at 11:59 PM PDT → October 12 at 08:59 AM CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST is UTC-8. Madrid in March 2026 will be on CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1 (daylight saving time in Spain starts the last Sunday of March, so on March 3 it's still standard time, UTC+1).

The difference between PST and CET is 9 hours (UTC+1 minus UTC-8 = +9 hours).

March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST → add 9 hours → March 4, 2026 at 08:59 AM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. Los Angeles in February is on PST, which is UTC-8. The difference is 9 hours (CET is 9 hours ahead of PST).

10:00 AM CET → subtract 9 hours → 1:00 AM PST (same date).

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9. Lima, Peru is UTC-5.

The difference is 9 - (-5) = 14 hours. Lima is 14 hours behind JST.

8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 → subtract 14 hours → 6:00 PM (18:00) on May 4, 2026 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) in late October will be PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7. (Note: the US switches from daylight saving time on November 1, 2026, so October 28 is still PDT.)

Madrid in late October: Spain switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So on October 28, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

Difference: UTC+1 minus UTC-7 = 8 hours ahead.

October 28 at 11:59 PM PT = October 29 at 07:59 AM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**ET (Eastern Time)** on October 30, 2026 — I need to check if it's EDT or EST.

- Daylight Saving Time in the US Eastern zone ends the first Sunday of November. In 2026, November 1 is a Sunday, so DST ends November 1, 2026.
- On October 30, 2026, the US is still on **EDT (UTC−4)**.

So 9:00 AM ET = 9:00 AM EDT = **13:00 UTC**.

**Madrid (Spain)** is on CET (UTC+1) in winter, but DST in Europe ends the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is **October 25, 2026**.

- So by October 30, 2026, Spain is already on **CET (UTC+1)**.

**Madrid local time:** 13:00 UTC + 1 hour = **14:00**

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00
